problem: Prior zero-shot VLN methods (LM-Nav, CLIP-Nav, CoW/ZSON-style decompositions) use an LLM to extract only the landmarks from an instruction and then navigate to the front of each one. They ignore the action attached to each landmark (e.g. 'exit the bedroom', 'go past the sofa') and so drive the agent the wrong way. Supervised continuous-VLN methods avoid this but need about 10K annotated path-instruction pairs.
motivation: Path-instruction annotation is expensive and does not scale to new scenes, so VLN ability should come from foundation models plus freely collected data. The authors observe that, for the same landmark, different action verbs put the landmark in different positions along the path: at the end for GoTo, in the middle for GoPast or GoThrough, at the start for Exit. This geometric regularity can be simulated by sampling paths and goal images, which yields action-specific training data with no language annotation.
key_idea: GPT-3 decomposes the instruction into a sequence of (Action, Landmark) sub-tasks. Each sub-task is executed by one of five action-specific CLIP-goal navigators, obtained by fine-tuning ZSON with RL on automatically generated image-path datasets in which the goal image is captured at the start, middle or end of the path depending on the action.
insight: Adding action-specific navigators on top of a plain GoTo (ZSON) navigator improves results monotonically (Table 2). R2R-Habitat SR goes 19.3→20.9→21.5→22.3→22.6 as GoPast, GoInto, GoThrough and Exit are added; on RxR-Habitat, adding GoThrough gives the largest jump (14.7→16.7). The sub-task evaluation on FG-R2R shows where the gain comes from: approach-the-landmark navigators fail on Exit (ZSON 13.0 SR, CoW 19.2), while the learned Exit navigator reaches 41.1 SR, so the direction relative to the landmark matters. Parser quality is also critical: GPT-3 with few-shot parsing examples reaches 22.6 SR; a heuristic grammatical parser gets 17.1, and adding a written sub-task definition to the prompt hurts (definition only 8.6, definition + examples 19.0).
method: Action-specific sub-task taxonomy: an instruction is represented as a sequence of (Action, Landmark) templates with five types, (GoTo, Object), (GoPast, Object), (GoInto, Region), (GoThrough, Region) and (Exit, Region); GoAway is dropped because it defines no destination.

LLM instruction parser: GPT-3 prompted with a few correct instruction-parsing examples (in-context learning) outputs the ordered sub-task list. Free-form actions that match no predefined type are mapped to the nearest type by BERT embedding cosine similarity ('semantic translation').

Action-specific image-path datasets: shortest paths are sampled in HM3D and the goal image is placed according to the action. GoPast: path >1.5 m, image mid-path facing the direction of travel with ±45° jitter. GoInto: start within 1.5 m of a region entrance, random goal inside the region. GoThrough: path from one entrance of a region to another, image mid-path. Exit: GoInto reversed, image at the path start. Entrances come from intersecting room-region bounding boxes with the occupancy map. GoPast uses 800 HM3D train scenes, the others use 131 region-annotated scenes; 9,000 pairs are sampled per scene.

Action-specific navigators: the ZSON image-goal policy (CLIP-encoded goal, config A agent) is fine-tuned separately on each dataset with DD-PPO for 100M steps, using the ZSON reward (success + angle-success + Δdistance + Δangle + slack −0.01). GoTo reuses the original ZSON model unchanged.

Zero-shot execution: at test time the landmark text is CLIP-encoded as the goal embedding and the navigator matching the current sub-task predicts low-level actions from 128×128 RGB. The agent switches to the next sub-task on STOP or after m_s steps (100 for R2R, 50 for RxR); the episode ends when all sub-tasks finish or after m_e = 500 steps.

setting.backbone: GPT-3 (frozen, prompted) as instruction parser + BERT for action mapping + ZSON policy (CLIP-encoded goal, DD-PPO-trained RL policy) fine-tuned into 5 action-specific navigators
setting.training_data: No path-instruction annotations. ZSON pretrained on HM3D image-goal episodes (config A), then fine-tuned with RL (DD-PPO, 100M steps each) on self-generated action-specific image-path datasets from HM3D: GoPast from 800 train scenes; GoInto/GoThrough/Exit from 131 scenes with room-region bounding-box annotations; 9,000 image-path pairs per scene.
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB only (128×128, 90° HFOV), no depth, no GPS/compass
setting.action_space: low-level STOP / FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN LEFT/RIGHT 30°
setting.simulator: Habitat (Matterport3D scenes for evaluation, HM3D for training)
setting.privileged: none at test time (training data generation uses room-region bounding-box annotations and navmesh shortest paths)

numbers_note: Comparison against supervised Seq2Seq and WS-MGMap re-trained on partial training data is shown only in a figure (Fig. 'Comparison with the supervised learning methods that are trained on partial training data'), with no numeric table. NE/OSR/nDTW are not reported. The agent config (RGB-only 128×128, 30° turns, 1.25 m height) differs from the standard VLN-CE setup, so comparison to other VLN-CE numbers is not exactly like-for-like.
results: A²Nav reaches 22.6 SR / 11.1 SPL on R2R-Habitat and 16.8 SR / 6.3 SPL on RxR-Habitat (English) val-unseen with no path-instruction annotation. It beats the strongest zero-shot baseline, ZSON with a GPT-3 decomposition (19.3/9.3 and 14.2/4.8), and CLIP-Nav, Seq CLIP-Nav and CoW by 14.8–17.0 SR on R2R. On RxR it exceeds supervised WS-MGMap in SR (16.8 vs 15.0) but not in SPL (6.3 vs 12.1), and on R2R it remains below supervised methods (Seq2Seq 25.0, WS-MGMap 38.9 SR).
limitations: Generating the action-specific datasets requires room-region bounding-box annotations, which restricts training to 131 region-annotated HM3D scenes for GoInto, GoThrough and Exit.
Absolute performance and especially efficiency are low (SPL 11.1 on R2R vs 34.3 for supervised WS-MGMap). The policy has no map or memory, and a GoAway-style action is not supported.

The evaluation agent config (RGB-only 128×128, 30° turns) is non-standard. Baselines CLIP-Nav, Seq CLIP-Nav and CoW were re-implemented with Habitat's oracle shortest-path follower, so the comparisons are not fully standard.
